text: It says hours. Plural. That's a suggestion.
note: Easy, packing up, completely sure, a little amused.

text: Who's Darnell?
note: Light, curious.

text: ...Pickup's at five.
note: A beat of unease, then brisk, changing the subject, leaving. Say every word clearly, including the last word, five.

text: No.
note: Flat, under his breath, refusing what he sees. Long cut only.

text: I did not RSVP to that.
note: Quiet, betrayed, offended, stressing RSVP.

text: I'm not even here.
note: Insisting, a little too fast, still sure he is leaving.

text: ...Not yet, bro.
note: Soft, kind, he cannot do it to him.

text: Prof. You're mogging the whole faculty. Everybody says it.
note: Leaning in, fully committed, hyping him up, sincere and confident. Start right on the first word.

text: Office hours.
note: Flat, hollow, a man who has seen things.

text: Great sesh, fam. Real ones come to office hours.
note: A soft, gentle whisper right into the mic, proud of saying fam; the room's PA makes it boom.

text: Do the students think I'm... HTN?
note: Very small, scared of the answer, lip trembling; HTN said as letters.

text: You're cooked.
note: Barely moving his lips, low, certain.

text: Where were you?
note: Normal, a bit annoyed, on the pitch.

text: Did they ever drop the new GTA?
note: Gentle, hopeful, like it's nothing.

text: Just go in, baby. It's faster.
note: Warm older woman, unbothered, mopping, not looking up. Long cut only.
